title: Superposition as Classical Hidden Variable / Coin in Flight
false_belief: A qubit in superposition is already in state 0 or 1, we just don't know which until we look.
refutation: A qubit in superposition has no definite classical value prior to measurement. The state |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ is a linear combination of physical statevectors with measurable interference effects.
distractor_hint: Remember: superposition is not incomplete information. The quantum state exhibits wave interference, which a classical coin with a hidden side cannot do.

title: Hadamard Creates Entanglement Alone
false_belief: Applying a Hadamard gate on a qubit creates entanglement.
refutation: The Hadamard gate is a single-qubit unitary rotation. Entanglement is a multi-qubit property that strictly requires two-qubit entangling gates (like CNOT, CZ, or SWAP) acting across non-separable Hilbert spaces.
distractor_hint: Single-qubit gates can never create entanglement! H on |0⟩ creates |+⟩ = (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2, which is a pure single-qubit superposition, not entangled.

title: Global Phase Has Observable Measurement Differences
false_belief: State -|0⟩ will yield different measurement probabilities than |0⟩.
refutation: Global phase e^(iθ) drops out of Born rule calculations: |e^(iθ)α|² = |e^(iθ)|²·|α|² = 1·|α|² = |α|². Only relative phase between basis states (|0⟩ + e^(iθ)|1⟩) alters interference and observable probabilities.
distractor_hint: Check the Born rule: P(x) = |⟨x|e^(iθ)ψ⟩|² = |e^(iθ)|²·|⟨x|ψ⟩|² = |⟨x|ψ⟩|². Global phases are physically undetectable.

title: Measurement Is Non-Invasive Observation
false_belief: Measuring a qubit reads its state without altering the underlying wave function.
refutation: Quantum measurement is a non-unitary projection. It irretrievably collapses the statevector into an eigenstate of the measurement operator, erasing prior superposition.
distractor_hint: Measurement in quantum mechanics is active and destructive: it collapses the superposition into a single eigenstate with probability given by the Born rule.

title: Entangled Qubits Have Surface Bloch Vectors
false_belief: Every qubit in an entangled pair has an arrow pointing to the surface of its individual Bloch sphere.
refutation: The state of a single qubit in an entangled system is described by a reduced density matrix with purity Tr(ρ²) < 1. In a maximally entangled Bell state, the individual subsystem is maximally mixed (ρ = I/2), and its Bloch vector shrinks to the origin (r = 0).
distractor_hint: When qubits are entangled, individual statevectors do not exist. Tracing out the other qubit yields a mixed state inside the Bloch sphere with radius r < 1.

title: Quantum States Can Be Copied Like Digital Files
false_belief: A quantum circuit can copy an unknown quantum state |ψ⟩ onto another qubit.
refutation: The No-Cloning Theorem proves that linearity and unitarity of quantum mechanics forbid any universal copying operator U such that U|ψ⟩|0⟩ = |ψ⟩|ψ⟩ for arbitrary |ψ⟩.
distractor_hint: By the No-Cloning Theorem, unknown quantum states cannot be duplicated. You can only transfer state via quantum teleportation, which destroys the original.

title: CNOT Always Flips the Target Qubit
false_belief: A CNOT gate always changes the state of the target qubit.
refutation: The CNOT gate acts conditionally: it applies an X gate to the target qubit if and only if the control qubit is in state |1⟩. If the control is |0⟩, the target is unchanged.
distractor_hint: Check the control qubit: CNOT only flips the target when the control state has amplitude on |1⟩.

title: Control Qubit Never Experiences Phase Shifts in Controlled Gates
false_belief: In a controlled gate, the control qubit only directs the target and is never modified itself.
refutation: In Phase Kickback, when the target qubit is in an eigenstate of the conditional gate (e.g. |-⟩ for X), the eigenvalue (-1) is kicked back to modulate the relative phase of the control qubit.
distractor_hint: Remember Phase Kickback: if the target is |-⟩ = (|0⟩ - |1⟩)/√2, applying CX kicks a -1 phase factor into the control qubit (|1⟩ ➔ -|1⟩).

title: Grover's Algorithm Provides Exponential Speedup
false_belief: Grover's search algorithm solves unstructured search in logarithmic time O(log N).
refutation: Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup O(√N) compared to classical O(N). Shor's algorithm provides exponential speedup for factoring, but Grover is strictly polynomial/quadratic.
distractor_hint: Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup (O(√N)), not an exponential one. It is optimal for unstructured search in Hilbert space.

title: Entanglement Enables Superluminal Communication
false_belief: Measuring one half of an entangled pair instantly transmits a message faster than light to the other party.
refutation: Although measurement outcomes are correlated across spacelike separations, each observer's local measurement results are completely random (50% 0, 50% 1). Information can only be decoded when measurement bases are compared using a classical channel (bounded by speed of light c).
distractor_hint: The No-Communication Theorem guarantees that entanglement cannot transmit classical bits faster than light. Local reduced density matrices remain unchanged by distant measurements.
